The statement signals pronounced near-term downside risks from COVID-19, but the Fed’s rapid move to the effective lower bound, large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repos, discount-window easing, and dollar swap lines align with the credit-channel literature (Bernanke–Gertler; Kashyap–Lamont–Stein; Oliner–Rudebusch) in lowering the external finance premium and supporting investment and spending. VAR evidence (Sims) and inflation-forecast-targeting frameworks (Svensson) suggest such easing can cushion output when inflation pressures are muted and expectations remain anchored, while balance-sheet tools at the ZLB address liquidity constraints and market functioning (liquidity effects). Overall tone: negative near term, but partially offset by forceful, textbook countercyclical policy support.
